        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

About Tracium

Tracium builds AI-assisted technical documentation software that turns complex manuals and engineering documents into structured, traceable information. Our initial focus is maritime, with applications across manufacturing, aerospace, and defence.

We combine document intelligence with S1000D authoring to help technical teams extract maintenance information, create documentation, and verify AI-generated suggestions against their sources.

Your role

You will own the AI capabilities behind our document intelligence platform—from understanding complex PDFs to extracting information that engineers can review and use.

What you’ll do

  • Build pipelines for document parsing, OCR, layout understanding, and extraction from text, tables, and diagrams.

  • Develop retrieval and AI workflows for technical question answering and maintenance information extraction.

  • Improve model performance, processing speed, and cost across cloud and private deployments.

  • Work with product and engineering colleagues to bring prototypes into production.

  • Experience delivering AI or machine learning systems into production.

Apply

If you're looking for a place where you can drive change and redefine how millions of people travel, Flix is the place where you can lead your journey!

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.


Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

Growth at Kraken is being rebuilt around an AI-native platform. Instead of people manually building audiences, writing copy, adjusting budgets, and scheduling sends, agents find opportunities, make decisions, and execute across paid, organic, and lifecycle channels. They learn from every result and keep going.

People still run the system. Operators use a central hub to set the rules the agents follow, review and approve what they produce, and handle exceptions when something doesn’t fit. The platform also has to work across many markets and languages, and it operates in a regulated industry, so there are compliance checks and approval steps built in.

The team is a small, cross-functional group of growth, product, and engineering people who build this platform and run it day to day. We ship often, learn fast, and raise the quality bar with every release. You will work most closely with the engineers building the platform, the product team defining how operators use it, and the operators who rely on it every day. QA and operations is how the whole team knows the platform can be trusted.

 

The opportunity

You will own day-to-day operations and QA for our internal growth platform. You test it, catch problems before our customers do, keep approvals and exception queues moving, and report on how it’s performing. You will work closely with product, engineering and operators to make sure the platform works and keeps working.

  • This is a hands-on, detail-focused role. You will spend your days in the product, testing what’s new, checking what should already work, and writing up what you find so it gets fixed.

  • Test the platform regularly. Cover new releases, rule changes, and edge cases, and run regression checks to make sure existing features still work.

  • Find bugs and document them clearly, with steps to reproduce, severity, and impact. Follow them through until engineering fixes them and you’ve verified the fix.

  • Monitor platform performance and agent activity, flag anything that looks wrong, and escalate it to the right person.

  • Work the approval queues daily. Keep items moving and make sure nothing is left unreviewed.

  • Check agent output against defined checklists and standards, and escalate anything unclear or risky.Note where flows are confusing or inconsistent, and flag them to the team.

  • Write and maintain documentation: test plans, QA checklists, runbooks, and release notes.

 

What you bring

  • Experience in QA, testing, operations, support, or analytics, ideally on a software product or complex system

  • Exceptional attention to detail. You notice what others miss and double-check your work.

  • A structured approach to testing. You can create and follow a test plan, and think about what could break.

  • Clear written communication. Your bug reports and documentation should be easy for anyone to follow.

  • Comfort with data. You can read a dashboard and tell when a number looks off.

  • Fast learner. You pick up new tools and systems quickly and ask thoughtful questions.

  • AI-native habits. You use AI tools in your own work every day, and you’re curious about where they get things wrong.

  • Prompt engineering curiosity, you don't need to be an engineer, but you are willing to learn how to communicate with AI systems precisely and improve their outputs

  • Reliability. You keep to a routine, keep your queues clear, and tell people early when something is stuck.

 

Nice to haves

  • Experience testing software products or AI and LLM-based tools

  • Familiarity with Jira, Mixpanel, or similar tools

  • Exposure to marketing, CRM, or lifecycle messaging workflows

  • Interest in fintech or crypto

We are the creators of Flipper Zero — a portable device for tech enthusiasts and engineers. It’s a gadget with an awesome community that brings together millions of people around the world.

We’re building a new product — Flipper One. It’s a full-featured ARM-based computer running Linux in a compact form factor, powered by the Rockchip RK3576 SoC.

We’ve decided to make the entire development process completely open and public. That’s why we’re looking for a Developer Portal & Community Manager to own and manage the entire Flipper One Developer Portal: maintaining the wiki, collecting tasks from all development teams, managing all GitHub projects and repositories, and proactively communicating with the community.

This role is perfect for you if you want to be close to the product, see firsthand how it’s built, and help turn that process into a clear and valuable entry point for the community. This is not a “content manager” role — you’ll need to fully understand the development process, track all ongoing tasks, and connect the team with the community to make things happen.

What is the Developer Portal?

The Developer Portal is a public wiki + a set of GitHub projects built around Flipper One. It documents how the project works as a whole, explains the architecture of its major subsystems, and provides contribution guides for the community — showing how people can contribute to each sub-project.

Anyone reading the Developer Portal wiki should come away with a complete understanding of the project structure, each feature, and what exactly we are building.

Requirements:

  • You write clearly, concisely, and without fluff, and can show examples of your work: guides, instructions, READMEs, how-tos, or similar materials

  • Basic understanding of hardware, software, and development workflows (Git, commits, branches, pull requests)

  • Able to explain complex technical topics in simple language and visualize them with flowchart sketches

  • Strong verbal communication skills; you know how to listen, ask precise questions, and quickly extract the key points from chaotic discussions

  • Keep communication with the community productive — without toxicity, unnecessary softness, or bureaucracy

  • Comfortable collaborating closely with engineers and navigating technical contexts

  • Discern useful feedback and constructive disagreement from noise and spam

Help put frontier AI to work in Defence

Cosine is a UK AI lab building models, applications and training infrastructure for mission-critical organisations.

We build coding agents that work across real software systems, specialised Lumen models, AI-native security products and the infrastructure needed to deploy advanced AI in demanding environments. Our customers include some of the world's largest enterprises, including organisations operating behind strict security, regulatory and technical constraints.

We're also training Lumen Sovereign, the first frontier large language model trained in the UK, with the support of the UK Government.

We're now looking for an Applied ML Technical Lead to help develop and deploy advanced AI capabilities for organisations operating in UK Defence and national security.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will work across machine learning development, deployment and customer-facing technical delivery. You may spend part of your time training and evaluating models on complex sensor data, and part of your time working with Defence stakeholders to understand operational needs, shape priorities and guide delivery.

___________________________________________________________________________

  • Build ML capabilities for real Defence problems

  • Design, build, train and evaluate machine learning models for challenging applied Defence and national security use cases.

  • Develop and improve model architectures, training pipelines, evaluation frameworks and inference systems.

  • Work with real-world and synthetic datasets to improve model accuracy, robustness and generalisation.

  • Translate research prototypes into reliable, deployable capabilities that operate within demanding technical and security constraints.

  • Work closely with Cosine's ML research and engineering teams while taking direct ownership of technical outcomes.

Lead technical delivery from prototype to deployment

  • Own the technical direction and day-to-day progress of applied ML projects.

  • Turn operational objectives into concrete technical goals, experiments, milestones and success measures.

  • Coordinate work across ML researchers, software engineers, infrastructure teams and external stakeholders.

  • Identify technical dependencies, delivery risks and blockers, and help drive them to resolution.

  • Establish clear evaluation criteria and demonstrate progress through measurable improvements and working capabilities.

  • Balance hands-on engineering with the planning and coordination needed to keep complex technical work moving.

Work directly with Defence customers

  • Engage with technical and operational stakeholders across the UK Defence and national security ecosystem.

  • Understand operational challenges and identify where machine learning can make a meaningful difference.

  • Translate customer requirements and constraints into technical objectives, datasets, experiments and delivery plans.

  • Present technical progress, demonstrate working capabilities and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Build trusted relationships with Defence stakeholders and act as a credible technical counterpart.

  • Help customers understand the practical considerations of integrating and deploying ML systems in their existing environments.

Turn research into operational capability

  • Help deploy ML models into real-world environments, including secure, on-premise and resource-constrained systems.

  • Work on model optimisation, inference performance, integration and reliability.

  • Develop robust approaches to evaluation, validation and continuous model improvement.

  • Understand data availability, access requirements, security restrictions and deployment constraints.

  • Establish feedback loops between operational users and Cosine's engineering teams.

  • Ensure that what we build is not only technically impressive, but genuinely useful to the people relying on it.

___________________________________________________________________________

What we’re looking for

You'll probably have a background in applied machine learning, ML engineering, research engineering or a similarly technical role, along with experience taking ownership of complex technical work.

You should be comfortable:

  • Writing production-quality Python and working with modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch.

  • Building, training, fine-tuning and evaluating machine learning models.

  • Working with complex datasets, designing experiments and interpreting model performance.

  • Understanding the trade-offs between model performance, compute requirements, latency and deployment constraints.

  • Working with engineering infrastructure, including Git, containers, Linux and GPU compute.

  • Taking technical ownership of projects with multiple stakeholders, uncertain requirements and evolving priorities.

  • Communicating technical concepts clearly to researchers, engineers, senior stakeholders and operational users.

  • Moving between model development, customer discussions and delivery planning without losing technical depth.

  • Making sound technical judgements, prioritising effectively and finding practical solutions when the path forward is unclear.

  • You don't need to have worked in Defence before. You do need to be excited by the opportunity to apply advanced ML to difficult, consequential real-world problems.

Nice to have

  • Existing UK security clearance, such as SC or DV, or previous experience working in secure Defence environments.

  • Experience with signal processing, time-series data, sensor fusion, representation learning or machine learning applied to complex real-world datasets.

  • Experience with foundation models, multimodal learning or advanced model training and post-training techniques.

  • Experience deploying ML models to edge devices or constrained compute environments.

  • Familiarity with UK Defence procurement, technical assurance or the national security landscape.

  • Experience leading technical workstreams or working as a technical lead on customer-facing ML projects.

___________________________________________________________________________

What success looks like

In your first three months, we would expect you to:

  • Become the technical lead for a major applied Defence ML programme, with responsibility for its day-to-day technical progress.

  • Build strong working relationships with Cosine's ML researchers, engineers and key Defence customer stakeholders.

  • Develop a clear understanding of the existing models, datasets, technical architecture and operational objectives.

  • Establish a focused delivery plan with clear priorities, milestones, ownership and success measures.

  • Make meaningful hands-on contributions to model development, evaluation or deployment.

  • Identify and begin addressing the most important technical and operational blockers.

  • Demonstrate tangible progress to customer stakeholders and build confidence in Cosine's ability to deliver.

  • Longer term, you'll help take advanced ML capabilities from promising prototypes into operational use, while shaping how Cosine builds and delivers applied AI for Defence and other mission-critical organisations.

Why this role matters

Some of the most important applications of AI won't be found in consumer products. They'll be in environments where information is incomplete, systems are complex, security matters and the consequences of getting things wrong are significant.

Cosine is working to bring frontier machine learning into those environments.

Doing that requires more than good models. It requires people who can understand an operational problem, build something that works, make good technical decisions, coordinate the work needed to deliver it and stay close to the customer until it creates real value.

You'll have unusual proximity to cutting-edge ML research, senior Defence stakeholders and the operational challenges that will shape the next generation of AI capabilities.

This role will suit someone who is technically strong enough to build, organised enough to lead technical delivery and curious enough to engage directly with the people using the technology.

If you enjoy being close to the research, close to customers and personally accountable for turning ambitious technology into something real, come and work with us.

Ingénieur R&D Conception d'équipements d’essais  (H/F)

À propos de notre client

Notre client est une TPE basée au nord de Lyon, spécialisée dans les énergies du sous-sol : pétrole, gaz, géothermie et stockage de CO2. Son activité repose entièrement sur la R&D : essais sur géomatériaux, géomécanique et développement d'équipements d'essais pour des clients internationaux.

Son équipe pluridisciplinaire et multiculturelle développe des solutions technologiques innovantes au service de l'efficacité, de la protection de l'environnement et de la maîtrise des coûts. L'entreprise est certifiée ISO 9001 et toutes ses activités respectent sa démarche QHSE.

Le poste

Pour accélérer ses projets de développement, notre client recrute un(e) Ingénieur(e) R&D en conception d'équipements d'essais.  Vous prendrez en charge la conception, la mise au point et la validation de cellules d'essais haute température et haute pression, un sujet stratégique pour l'entreprise et ses clients.

Rattaché(e) à la direction des opérations, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe qui conçoit aujourd'hui les équipements et dépose les brevets de l'entreprise.

Répartition indicative du temps : environ 70 à 80 % conception et développement, 20 à 30 % laboratoire (montage et validation de vos équipements).

Dans une structure à taille humaine, vous suivrez vos développements de la conception jusqu'aux tests, avant leur transfert à l'équipe de production.

Vos missions

Conception et développement d'équipements d’essais

  • Concevoir de nouvelles cellules et de nouveaux dispositifs d'essais, notamment pour des conditions de haute température et de haute pression.
  • Résoudre les problématiques techniques associées : instrumentation et capteurs, étanchéité, tenue en température et en pression.
  • Consulter les fournisseurs et sous-traitants, et suivre la fabrication des pièces.
  • Améliorer les équipements existants, notamment leur ergonomie et leur facilité d'utilisation en production.

Mise au point et validation

  • Monter les équipements développés et réaliser leurs tests de validation au laboratoire.
  • Interpréter les résultats expérimentaux et vérifier leur cohérence.
  • Transférer les équipements validés à l'équipe de production et l'accompagner dans leur prise en main.

Documentation et propriété intellectuelle

  • Rédiger la documentation technique, les rapports et les comptes-rendus, et les présenter, en français comme en anglais.
  • Participer à la veille technique et à la rédaction des documents de protection (brevets, enveloppes Soleau).

Vie du laboratoire

  • Comprendre les essais réalisés au laboratoire pour concevoir des équipements adaptés à leurs besoins.
  • Contribuer à l'activité du labo et à l'amélioration continue, dans le respect de la démarche qualité ISO 9001.

Requirements

Compétences techniques

  • Conception mécanique et maîtrise d'un logiciel de CAO.
  • Instrumentation, capteurs et techniques de mesure.
  • Compréhension des grandeurs physiques et physico-chimiques.
  • Rédaction technique et anglais professionnel, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Savoir-être

  • Autonomie et capacité à prendre en main un sujet de bout en bout.
  • Rigueur, notamment dans les phases d'essais.
  • Polyvalence et goût du concret : vous aimez concevoir autant que tester vous-même vos équipements.
  • Communication proactive, en particulier pour remonter et résoudre les difficultés rencontrées.
  • Envie d'apprendre et de s'investir dans une petite structure.

Formation et expérience

  • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou équivalent Bac +5 en génie mécanique, conception, instrumentation ou mesures physiques.
  • Expérience d'environ 5 ans en conception d'équipements, en bureau d'études ou en R&D. Les profils plus juniors avec une première expérience significative en conception seront étudiés.
  • Une expérience sur des équipements soumis à des contraintes de température ou de pression est un vrai plus.

Benefits

Vous rejoindrez une entreprise à taille humaine où chaque développement compte : vos équipements seront directement utilisés pour des projets de R&D menés pour des clients internationaux. Vous travaillerez au sein d'une équipe dynamique et multiculturelle, sur des sujets techniques exigeants au service des énergies du sous-sol et de la transition énergétique.

    • Share expertise, lessons learned, and best practices to strengthen team capability, collaboration, product quality, reliability, and continuous improvement.

    ·        Beheer, licenties en onderhoud van computers, software en mobiele apparatuur;

    ·        Netwerk en technische ICT-ondersteuning (incl. windtunnel testomgeving, data backup incl. meetdata);

    ·        Cybersecurity en informatiebeveiliging. Data security en privacy. Binnen het team zijn ook de rollen Security Officer (DWN breed NL + DE)  en IT Security Officer (locaties Amsterdam en Marknesse)  gepositioneerd.

    Specifieke verantwoordelijkheden van de teamleider:

    ·        Aansturen, coachen en ontwikkelen van het team.

    ·        Ontwikkelen, adviseren over en uitvoeren van de ICT- en securityvisie en -strategie.

    ·        Zorgen voor de randvoorwaarden waarbinnen de Security Officer en IT Security Officer hun verantwoordelijkheden onafhankelijk en effectief kunnen uitvoeren.

    ·        Coördineren van ICT- en securityprojecten en verbetertrajecten inclusief afstemming met alle stakeholders binnen DNW, inclusief de Duitse locaties.

    ·        Zorgen voor passende processen rondom incidenten, wijzigingen en risico’s binnen de organisatie.

    ·        Bewaken van de aansluiting op relevante wet- en regelgeving en interne beleidskaders.

    Wie ben jij?

    Je bent een verbindende en resultaatgerichte teamleider die begrijpt dat ICT en security geen doel op zich zijn, maar randvoorwaarden voor een goed functionerende organisatie.

    Je combineert een mensgerichte leiderschapsstijl met voldoende inhoudelijke kennis en organisatiesensitiviteit.     • Ervaring met het aansturen en ontwikkelen van medewerkers en teams.

    • Goede communicatieve en organisatorische vaardigheden.

    • Een pragmatische, verbindende en oplossingsgerichte houding.

    • Goede beheersing van Nederlands, Engels en bij voorkeur ook de Duitse taal

    Wat bieden wij jou?

    Werken bij DNW, betekent werken in een nationale en internationale hightech omgeving. Samenwerken en betrokkenheid staan bij ons hoog in vaandel. Door jou vrijheid en eigen verantwoordelijkheid te geven, ben jij het best in staat om tot baanbrekende innovaties te komen. Wil jij jezelf vakinhoudelijk én op persoonlijk vlak ontwikkelen?     De Duits-Nederlands Windtunnels (DNW) exploiteert zes wind tunnels op vier verschillende locaties van het Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum (NLR) en van de Duitse zusterorganisatie DLR. XXIX — Design When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

Plus, our partner organizations

  • Lightphone

  • IngredientAI

 

🔮 Who we’re looking for:

  • Collaborating closely with Technical Leads and Designers to meet clients' custom e-commerce and technical needs.
  • Building and maintaining high-performance storefronts using both custom Liquid (Online Store 2.0) and modern headless architectures (Shopify Storefront API, GraphQL, Hydrogen/Remix, Next.js).
  • Implementing responsive, accessible, and pixel-perfect interfaces based on design specifications, with meticulous attention to product interaction details and motion design.
  • Integrating custom storefronts with headless CMS platforms (Sanity, Contentful), payment gateways, subscriptions, search, and third-party e-commerce APIs.
  • Optimizing e-commerce performance, focusing heavily on Core Web Vitals, image/video asset delivery, bundle size, and runtime efficiency across high-traffic collection and product pages.
  • Architecting scalable, reusable component libraries and design systems tailored for commercial platforms.
  • Writing clear documentation for store management, custom app integrations, and codebase maintenance.
  • Participating in project team rituals, including Sprint Planning, daily standups, code reviews, and retrospectives.

The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart”, by carefully managing their workflow and staggering features that have dependencies intelligently. They prefer deep work but are OK coming up to the surface now and then for top level / strategic conversations.

🔑 Must-Have Competencies:

  • 8+ years writing highly performant frontend code with an obsession for 95+ Lighthouse scores and optimal Core Web Vitals.
  • Deep Shopify Ecosystem Mastery: Proven experience building custom Shopify themes (Liquid, JSON templates, Online Store 2.0) as well as headless storefronts using the Shopify Storefront API (GraphQL) and frameworks like Hydrogen/Remix or Next.js.
  • Modern Frontend Tech: Expert-level experience with TypeScript and modern CSS methodologies (Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules) alongside robust animation libraries (GSAP, Framer Motion).
  • Headless CMS & Integrations: Extensive experience merging Shopify with headless CMS platforms like Sanity, Contentful, or Prismic, as well as third-party services (Klaviyo, Recharge, Algolia/Searchspring, Stripe).
  • Platform & Hosting: Fluency in industry-standard PaaS platforms including Vercel, Netlify, and Shopify Oxygen.
  • Architecture & State Management: Experience with state management solutions (Zustand, Redux, Pinia) and API integration patterns for cart state, multi-currency, and checkout flows.
  • Quality & Accessibility: Experience building accessible (WCAG compliant), responsive interfaces with a strong commitment to SEO best practices, testing frameworks (Jest, Playwright, Cypress), and maintainable code.
  • Performance Optimization: Practical knowledge of WebSockets, caching strategies (Redis, CDN-level/Cloudflare), and advanced image delivery networks.

 

💪 Nice-to-Have Competencies:

  • Custom App Development: Building bespoke Shopify Apps using Node.js, Remix, GraphQL Admin API, and Shopify CLI.
  • Shopify Plus & Enterprise Features: Hands-on experience with Shopify Functions, Checkout Branding API, Shopify Scripts, and B2B configurations.
  • Tracking & Analytics: Setting up server-side tracking, GTM, Meta Pixel, and Customer Privacy APIs without hurting site load times.
  • WebGL, Canvas & 3D: Experience building interactive graphics, 3D product visualizers, or canvas animations using Three.js or ``.
  • Full-Stack & API Design: Experience across backend/database layers (PostgreSQL), REST/GraphQL API design, and authentication flows (OAuth, JWT).

💸 Compensation

Our pay scale ranges from $40/hr to $120/hr pending seniority (& team leadership experience), and our projects are rarely less than 8 full time weeks at 40 hours per week.

  • Transparency & Ownership: We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.

Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.

Who We Are

Goodway Group is one of AdAge's 2026's BEST PLACES TO WORK! As an independent and remote-first media and marketing services firm with a 90+ year history, Goodway Group has the security of an established company combined with a start-up feel. With leading data-driven and technology-enabled digital media and marketing services firm with teams in the U.S. and the UK, our diverse team of digital strategists, media practitioners, technologists and data scientists have won the most prestigious awards for innovative marketing technology, impactful work and inclusive remote-first places to work including being honored as a multiyear winner in Ad Age Best Places to Work, Ad Exchanger's Best Use of Technology by an Agency Award and two MarTech Breakthrough Awards and a certified service partner to The Trade Desk.

The Paid Media Manager is responsible for the strategic planning, activation, optimization, and management of social programmatic media campaigns. This role translates client communication strategies, customer journeys, audience insights, and business objectives into effective media activation plans.

The ideal candidate has strong experience managing performance-focused social campaigns, particularly through programmatic buying environments. Experience supporting commerce, retail media, direct-response, or growth-focused clients is required. Paid search experience is helpful but not required.

What You’ll Do 

Strategic Media Activation:

  • Plan, activate, optimize, and manage social programmatic media campaigns aligned with client objectives, audience insights, and customer journeys.
  • Develop campaign structures, audience strategies, investment plans, bidding approaches, placement strategies, and testing frameworks.
  • Execute and optimize campaigns across social and programmatic platforms, including relevant DSPs, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Snapchat, and other emerging platforms.
  • Make activation and investment decisions based on business goals, audience behavior, campaign performance, and available client or proprietary data.
  • Manage performance against metrics such as reach, frequency, CTR, conversion rate, CPL, CPA, CAC, ROAS, and other client-specific KPIs.
  • Apply a test-and-learn approach across audiences, creative, placements, bidding strategies, inventory, frequency, and campaign structure.
  • Oversee the full campaign lifecycle, including setup, trafficking, QA, optimization, troubleshooting, reporting, forecasting, and billing.
  • Ensure brand safety, fraud prevention, viewability, tracking accuracy, and data-quality transparency across campaigns.
  • Support audits of prospective and existing client social and programmatic accounts.
  • Identify opportunities to expand campaigns, test new buying strategies, and improve efficiency and scale.

Client Service:

  • Develop comprehensive social programmatic activation plans aligned with each client’s business goals and customer journey.
  • Translate media objectives and strategic recommendations into clear social and programmatic campaign plans.
  • Anticipate client needs and provide proactive, data-informed recommendations.
  • Present campaign performance, analysis, and insights to clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Explain platform strategies, investment decisions, results, and optimization recommendations in clear business terms.
  • Build trusted client relationships through responsive communication, reliable execution, and strategic guidance.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Collaborate with strategy, planning, analytics, creative, CX, investment, and account teams to deliver a cohesive consumer experience.
  • Work closely with media planning teams to manage campaign delivery and provide ongoing optimization recommendations.
  • Coordinate creative requirements, tracking needs, reporting expectations, and campaign timelines across internal and client teams.
  • Contribute social programmatic expertise to broader media planning discussions, business reviews, and client presentations.
  • Support and mentor junior team members by sharing platform knowledge, activation standards, and optimization best practices.

Thought-Leadership:

  • Help establish and refine social programmatic activation standards, processes, and best practices.
  • Stay current on platform changes, privacy developments, measurement capabilities, inventory quality, emerging technologies, and industry trends.
  • Identify new buying strategies, platform capabilities, audience solutions, and testing opportunities that may improve client outcomes.
  • Contribute to team learning, professional development, and subject-matter expertise.

What You Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, advertising, business, or a related field preferred.
  • Three to five years of experience in social media activation, programmatic media, performance marketing, or a related discipline.
  • Hands-on experience planning, activating, optimizing, and reporting on social programmatic campaigns.
  • Experience working with commerce, retail media, direct-response, or growth-focused clients required.
  • Experience with one or more DSPs and social advertising platforms such as Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Snapchat, or X.
  • Strong understanding of audience strategy, campaign structure, bidding, budget allocation, inventory selection, forecasting, testing, optimization, reporting, troubleshooting, and billing.
  • Knowledge of pixels, conversion tracking, attribution, brand safety, fraud prevention, viewability, and data-quality standards.
  • Experience analyzing campaign data using tools such as Google Analytics, Looker Studio, Tableau, Skai, or similar platforms. SQL experience is a plus.
  • Paid search experience, including Google Ads or Microsoft Advertising, is helpful but not required.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate performance data into clear recommendations.
  • Excellent client communication and presentation skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple campaigns, platforms, priorities, and deadlines.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor junior team members and contribute to activation standards.
  • Collaborative approach and experience working effectively across strategy, planning, analytics, creative, CX, and investment teams.
  • Strong knowledge of social programmatic trends, buying practices, measurement approaches, and emerging technologies.

Important Note

This is a paid media activation role. It is not an organic social media, community management, or content publishing position. Candidates should have hands-on experience buying and optimizing paid social or social programmatic media.

Senior Customer Service Lead & Trainer – Team Leadership & Customer Experience | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours (EST)

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an experienced Senior Customer Service Lead & Trainer to lead, coach, and develop a remote customer support team serving U.S.-based customers.

This is more than a traditional customer service position. You’ll take ownership of team performance, employee training, quality assurance, escalations, and overall customer experience.

You’ll ensure agents consistently deliver professional, efficient, and high-quality support across phone, email, chat, and other digital channels while using coaching and performance data to continuously improve the team.

If you’re an experienced customer service leader who knows how to develop people, improve performance, maintain accountability, and build strong service standards, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

Team Leadership & Performance

  • Lead and manage a distributed customer service team
  • Monitor agent productivity, quality, attendance, and KPI performance
  • Conduct regular one-on-one coaching and performance reviews
  • Provide clear, actionable feedback to improve performance
  • Hold team members accountable to service and productivity standards
  • Identify performance gaps and implement improvement plans
  • Track progress following coaching and corrective actions
  • Build a consistent, accountable, and high-performing remote team culture

Training & Onboarding

  • Own onboarding and training for new customer service hires
  • Develop and maintain:
    • Training materials
    • Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
    • Call scripts
    • Customer service guidelines
    • Quality standards
  • Conduct structured training and coaching sessions
  • Review calls and customer interactions to identify training opportunities
  • Ensure new hires are fully prepared before independently handling customers
  • Continuously improve training programs based on recurring performance gaps

Quality Assurance & Coaching

  • Conduct regular call reviews and QA evaluations
  • Monitor adherence to scripts, processes, and customer experience standards
  • Identify recurring quality issues across the team
  • Coach agents on:
    • Communication
    • Professionalism
    • Problem-solving
    • Customer handling
    • Process adherence
  • Track improvement following coaching sessions
  • Maintain consistent QA standards across the customer support operation

Customer Experience & Escalations

  • Handle complex or escalated customer concerns professionally
  • Ensure customers receive consistent support across:
    • Phone
    • Email
    • Chat
    • Other digital communication channels
  • Maintain high standards for tone, responsiveness, and professionalism
  • Identify recurring customer pain points and recommend improvements
  • Help resolve operational issues affecting customer satisfaction
  • Support agents in navigating difficult or sensitive customer situations

Customer Support Operations & Reporting

  • Track and report on:
    • Customer satisfaction
    • Response times
    • Resolution rates
    • Agent productivity
    • QA scores
    • Training performance
  • Maintain accurate documentation and operational records
  • Use customer service platforms, VOIP systems, ticketing tools, and reporting systems effectively
  • Identify trends and recurring performance issues through support data
  • Collaborate with other departments to resolve recurring customer or operational issues

Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in customer service leadership, support supervision, or customer operations management
  • Proven experience managing remote and/or offshore customer service teams
  • Strong experience with employee coaching, training, and performance management
  • Experience conducting call reviews and quality assurance evaluations
  • Strong escalation management and customer problem-solving skills
  • Excellent spoken and written English
  • Strong organizational and multitasking abilities
  • Experience working with:
    • Customer support platforms
    • VOIP systems
    • Ticketing systems
    • Digital communication tools
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment
  • Ability to work U.S. EST business hours

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting U.S.-based customers
  • Background in:
    • Facility Management
    • Energy
    • Tech-enabled services
  • Experience working in startup or high-growth environments
  • Experience scaling customer support teams
  • Strong knowledge of KPI-driven customer service operations
  • Experience developing:
    • SOPs
    • QA scorecards
    • Training programs
    • Coaching frameworks

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Know how to lead and develop people, not simply supervise them
  • Can give direct, constructive feedback professionally
  • Hold team members accountable while maintaining strong morale
  • Stay calm and solutions-focused during difficult escalations
  • Have high standards for customer communication and service quality
  • Understand how to use QA and performance data to improve agent performance
  • Are highly organized and consistent with follow-through
  • Can effectively manage a distributed team without constant oversight
  • Know how to turn recurring performance issues into structured coaching and training opportunities

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may start by reviewing team performance, attendance, customer service KPIs, and any outstanding escalations.

You’ll listen to calls, complete QA evaluations, coach agents on communication and performance, and conduct onboarding or training sessions where needed.

Throughout the day, you may handle escalated customer concerns, review response and resolution times, identify recurring service issues, update SOPs or scripts, and coordinate with internal teams on operational improvements.

You’ll also monitor agents requiring additional coaching and ensure improvement plans are producing measurable results.

In short: you ensure the customer service team is well-trained, accountable, consistent, and capable of delivering an excellent customer experience.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Customer Satisfaction (CSAT)
  • Quality assurance scores
  • Response and resolution times
  • Agent productivity
  • Training and onboarding effectiveness
  • Escalation resolution rates
  • Process and SOP adherence
  • Performance improvement following coaching
  • Overall team reliability and consistency

Why This Role Stands Out

  • High ownership over customer service quality and team performance
  • Direct influence on how agents are trained, coached, and developed
  • Opportunity to shape QA standards and training systems
  • Leadership responsibility within a growing remote support environment
  • Strong visibility across operations and customer experience
  • Career growth opportunities into:
    • Customer Support Manager
    • Head of Customer Experience
    • Training & Quality Manager
    • Customer Operations Leadership

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application
  2. Spark Hire One-Way Video Interview
  3. Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  4. Practical Assessment
  5. Client Interview
  6. Offer & Onboarding

Spark Hire Video Interview – Required

As part of the application process, all candidates are required to complete a one-way video interview through Spark Hire.

After completing the first step of your application, you’ll receive a Spark Hire invitation by email with instructions to record and submit your video responses.

Completion of the Spark Hire video is required to be considered for the next stage. Please check your inbox as well as your spam or junk folder for the invitation.

Apply Now

If you have extensive customer service leadership experience and enjoy coaching teams, improving service quality, developing training programs, and building accountable support operations, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and take ownership of a remote customer service team where your leadership will directly influence both agent performance and the customer experience.

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

We're seeking a talented and motivated full-time Program Manager to join our team. This is a tactical, implementation-focused role, hands-on in shaping how EPD (Engineering, Product & Design) operates, works together, and stays productive: building and refining the processes and rhythms that keep the org running, driving improvement initiatives over time, and owning the processes behind EPD's operational health. You'll help the team understand trends and spot where improvements are needed.

Because we're an early-stage and fully remote company, we're looking for an individual who can work independently to align the teams involved in building the product. A deep understanding of the technical engineering space (how engineering teams operate, where the friction points typically live, and what good looks like) is essential to being effective and credible in this role. Ability to think on one's feet, enjoy collaborating with highly technical teams, operate comfortably in ambiguity without a clearly defined deliverable, and be comfortable working asynchronously is essential.

Key Responsibilities

You will work as part of the TPM team to:

  • Own the processes for bug tracking, incidents, reliability, and escalations, and continuously improve them to drive efficiency and progress toward EPD's operational health goals.
  • Spot trends across operational health data and translate them into clear insights on how EPD is doing and where improvement is needed.
  • Build dashboards and reports in tools like Jira and Snowflake that give EPD and the broader company visibility into operational health and progress.
  • Turn data into a clear story: what it's telling us, why it matters, and what needs to change, then design and implement the process changes to act on it.
  • Identify process gaps with EPD and proactively develop just the right amount of process to fill the gap: not too much, not too little.
  • Support planning activities and project tracking processes, helping keep them running smoothly and consistently across EPD.
  • Help run project status reviews, leadership roadmap reviews, and priority reviews, making sure the right information is ready and the right people are in the room.
  • Connect the dots across systems, processes, and teams, spotting where disconnected efforts overlap, conflict, or could be simplified, and acting on it.
  • Jump in on whatever initiative pops up in EPD that needs support, structure, or someone to help carry it forward, whether or not it fits inside a defined program.
  • Handle project retrospectives involving participants and stakeholders to understand what went well and what should be adjusted in future project work.
  • Seek opportunities to bring about ongoing improvement and simplification in business operating procedures and practices, leading to improved efficiency and effectiveness.

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience as a Program Manager or Technical Program Manager (TPM), coordinating with stakeholders and cross-functional teams, particularly experience working closely within Engineering and with Product.
  • Experience as a Program/Technical Program Manager in a remote startup environment
  • A deep, working understanding of the technical engineering space, including how engineering teams operate day to day, common workflows and tooling, and where technical and process friction tend to show up.
  • Experience owning operational health processes, such as bug tracking, incidents, reliability, or escalations, and using them to drive measurable efficiency gains.
  • Strong data skills, including building dashboards and reports in tools like Jira and Snowflake, and a solid understanding of how to read and interpret data.
  • Ability to spot trends in data and translate them into a clear story: what's happening, why it matters, and what should change, paired with the ability to design and implement the process changes needed to act on it.
  • Experience supporting planning cycles, project tracking, and recurring reviews, such as project status reviews or leadership roadmap and priority reviews.
  • A comfort level with ambiguity and undefined deliverables. You're motivated by taming chaos and improving how things run, not just shipping a fixed checklist.
  • A tactical, execution-first orientation: you're energized by hands-on implementation and getting things done, more than by high-level strategy or planning alone.
  • Experience working with Engineering, Product, and Design leadership, understanding their motivations and priorities, and using that to help move initiatives forward and communicate goals across the company.
  • Ability to give and process constructive feedback, as well as work independently.
  • Ability to communicate openly, supporting and championing innovation and inclusivity, in both written and verbal communication.
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies and project management tools, such as Jira, Notion and GitHub.
  • Familiarity with technical solutions, engineering practices, and the security and engineering lifecycle.
